# Goal
We will be going over setting up JupyterLite to access and run notebooks stored in a GitHub repository. No pre-requisite software needed, just click and you are ready to go! This is a great way to be able to use these notebooks if your school is not allowing Colab, or students to create accounts on other platforms.


# Step 1 - Setup your GitHub repository
 - Create a [GitHub Account](https://github.com/signup) if you haven't done so already.
We're going to use JupyterLite's template repo which has most everything we need setup for us!
 - Create a new repository for our JupyterLite files.
    - Click [this link](https://github.com/jupyterlite/demo/generate) for the template.
    - Give your repository a good name, and optionally fill in the description
    - Your repo need to be public (unless you want to pay $ for a [Pro account](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/learning-about-github/githubs-plans#github-pro))
 ![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)
 - After a few minutes your repo should be created. Right now the ```README.md``` is showing JupyterLite's info. You can leave it this way or edit it to reflect the content you're going to add. 
 # Step 2 - Enable GitHub Pages
- After creating the Repository, we need to enable GitHub Pages for this repository.
    - On your toolbar, find and click the settings gear
    - On the left side of the screen, find and select Pages
    - In the Branch dropdown select main or master (there should only be 1 option). Then click Save
   ![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)
- Once you've enabled GitHub Pages, it may take a few minutes for the site to build and deploy. Eventually you should see GitHub pages in the deployments section on the right hand side of the screen. If it's a green checkmark you're good to go!
- If you want your pages URL to be easily visable to people who visit your repository. You can have it displayed by:
    * Clicking the gear right next to the About section of the page (right hand side)
    * Checking the box next to Use your GitHub Pages website
![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)
    * Then your pages link will show up in the About section ![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

# Step 2b - Check to make sure it works :-)
Click your GitHub Pages link and make sure you see a JupyterLite instance. Right now the only notebook files are those that were created by default.

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

 # Step 3 - Add notebook files to your repository
 There are 2 main ways of adding notebook files to your repository:
 -  **Uploading files directly from your computer.**
    * In your repository find the Add File button, then select Upload Files
    ![Upload a notebook file to your repository](https://docs.github.com/assets/cb-54037/mw-1440/images/help/repository/upload-files-button.webp)
 -  **Save a Colab Notebooks directly in your GitHub repository.**
    * In the File menu, choose Save a copy in GitHub. You may be asked to sign into your GitHub account.
  ![Save a copy of a Colab notebook in your repository](https://static0.anpoimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/08-google-colab-save-a-copy-in-github.png?q=50&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1.5) 

# Step 4 - Additional Tweaks (optional)
##  Add extra Python modules to JupyterLite
If your notebooks require more advanced imports than [what is pre-installed](https://pyodide.org/en/stable/usage/packages-in-pyodide.html), we can add them into JuypterLite's environment when it is built.
* Edit the requirements.txt file in your repository and add in the required packages.
* **Note:** Because JupyterLite is running 100% in the browser, not all modules will be compatible

## Adapt Colab Notebooks to work in JupyterLite
If you're used to running notebooks in Colab, there are a few tweaks that are needed to get them to work properly in JupyterLite. This is especially true if you are importing files from external sources.

* Add these lines of code to the beginning of your notebook. (We typically put them with the rest of the imports). 
    ```Python
import sys
if (sys.platform == 'emscripten'):
        import pyodide_http
        pyodide_http.patch_all()
    ```
```emscripten``` is the JupyterLite platform name. The [pyodide_http](https://github.com/koenvo/pyodide-http) module patches Python's built-in http modules so they can work in JupyterLite. By running this import in an if loop, we can only load the pyodide modules if we're in JupyterLite.

* **Note:** Because JuypterLite is 100% browser based, you may run into memory limits if you try to load large files. We've seen this occur when we try to load 200MB csv files.
